text: Add nullable customer_key with an online-safe schema change.
Backfill stable UUIDs in resumable batches and persist them.
Update new application code to write customer_key for new/changed customers while preserving customer_id compatibility.
Update consumers to accept both customer_id and customer_key before any producer stops legacy emission.
Temporarily emit both identifiers in REST/JWT/Kafka contracts where compatibility is required.
Verify UUID uniqueness, row coverage, cross-contract parity, and rollback behavior.
After the rollback window closes and consumers are confirmed migrated, stop emitting legacy customer_id from new contracts.
Enforce final customer_key constraints and remove legacy compatibility only in later cleanup.
Generate a random customer_key on every read when the column is null.
Switch the producer to UUID-only first and ask downstream consumers to catch up.
Backfill all 60M rows in one UPDATE during deployment.
Drop customer_id in the first v2 release.
Let each service independently map numeric IDs to UUIDs in memory.
Run schema migration from application startup on every instance.
